chunks: Ishaq ibn 'Ammar asked Abā 'Abdillāh عليه السلام.
About a man who entrusted another man with one thousand dirhams, and they were lost. Then the man said to him: it was only a loan upon him, while the other said: it was only a deposit.
So he عليه السلام said: The money is binding upon him unless he establishes proof that it was only a deposit.

key_terms.أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ: one thousand dirhams, the amount in dispute
key_terms.الْمَالُ لَازِمٌ لَهُ: the money remains binding upon him as a liability
key_terms.اِسْتَوْدَعَ: entrusted someone with property for safekeeping
key_terms.قَرْضًا: a loan for which repayment is due

ai.seo_question: If money is lost and there is a dispute over whether it was a loan or a deposit, who is legally liable?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling in a dispute over whether transferred money was a loan or a deposit. The Imam عليه السلام rules that liability remains upon the holder of the money unless he can produce evidence proving that it was a deposit.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4092 - Ishaq ibn Ammar asked Abu Abdullah (as)

about a man who entrusted another man with one thousand dirhams, but the money was lost.
The trustee claimed that the amount was a loan, while the depositor insisted it was a deposit (wadi'ah).
Imam (as) said: "The money is binding upon him (the trustee) unless he provides evidence that it was a deposit."
